entries.title: Async I/O buffer/control-block lifetime: memory must remain valid until completion

provenance.publication: Boost.Asio official docs (buffer debugging overview); POSIX aio_read(3) man page; io_uring_enter(2) man page

sources.note: 'you need to ensure that the buffers for the operation are valid until the completion handler is called'
NOTES: 'The buffer area being read into must not be accessed during the operation or undefined results may occur.' / 'The memory areas involved must remain valid.'
IORING_OP_SEND_ZC: 'The user must not modify the data buffer until the notification is posted.'

normalized_semantic_trace: resource R (caller buffer or aio control block) exists in owner scope
async operation O is initiated against R; O borrows R by contract
O remains in flight beyond owner's local scope
owner destroys, moves, or mutates R
completion/backend later accesses R
invalid memory access or stale/corrupted data
preconditions: operation outstanding past owner scope exit
no runtime check ties buffer lifetime to operation lifetime
entries.race_or_failure_window: from operation submission until its completion handler/terminal
entries.bad_outcome: use-after-free / use-after-move of the borrowed buffer
entries.externally_observable_effect: memory corruption, wrong data delivered, ASan-reported UAF, potential exploitation
entries.silent_or_distributed_character: silent unless sanitizer instrumented; window is temporal and crosses thread boundary
entries.conventional_obligation: undocumented-in-types caller discipline: keep buffer + control block alive/unmodified until completion; enforced only by docs and programmer memory
entries.sluice_protocol_obligation: caller-owned Completion + explicit borrow contract for the request lifetime (ADR-explicit-io-request-contract); borrow must stay alive and address-stable for the bounded request lifecycle
entries.evidence_for_status: The obligation is explicit in the public contract (completion.hpp caller-owned Completion; borrow rules in docs/architecture), but a caller who destroys the borrowed buffer while a request is outstanding is not detected by Sluice itself; detection is left to external tooling (ASan) or code review. No repository witness shows Sluice fail-fast on this violation.
entries.comparison_notes: Obligation representation is fair (both document the lifetime duty); detection is not: Sluice adds no runtime/compile-time check for borrow lifetime, so the hazard's bad_outcome is equivalent risk under Sluice. Recorded as a priority §16 silent case.
se2_probe_candidates: ASan on a deliberate borrower-destroys-buffer probe under ThreadPool/Uring backends
negative-compile feasibility for borrowed-buffer lifetime annotations
entries.notes: Documented contract hazard, not a single historical incident; per task §13 a generic UAF would be insufficient — the three sources above all tie lifetime causally to in-flight async operation.

normalized_semantic_trace: std::string buf allocated on stack
async_read(socket, asio::buffer(buf), handler) initiated
function returns before completion; buf destroyed
operation completes into freed stack memory
handler reads bytes_transferred into dead object
preconditions: initiating scope exits before completion

entries.externally_observable_effect: garbage data, ASan stack-use-after-return, crash
entries.silent_or_distributed_character: silent in ordinary builds; classic single-producer single-completion window
entries.conventional_obligation: same as SE1-CA-H01-1

entries.title: Identity reuse without generation: reusing an in-flight async control block (ABA on request identity)

provenance.publication: POSIX aio_read(3) man page (as implemented by glibc/Linux man-pages)

sources.note: NOTES: 'The control block must not be changed while the read operation is in progress.' / 'Simultaneous I/O operations specifying the same aiocb structure produce undefined results.'

normalized_semantic_trace: request identity slot S is occupied by in-flight operation O1
caller cannot distinguish 'S busy' from 'S free' (identity is a bare pointer/struct)
caller reuses S for operation O2 (or mutates S in place)
backend still holds references keyed only on S
completion or cancellation intended for O1 is applied to O2 (or UB)
wrong result, lost cancellation, or undefined behavior
preconditions: identity is caller-visible and reusable without a generation/stamp
entries.race_or_failure_window: between O1 still being referenced and S being reused
entries.bad_outcome: ABA: stale completion/cancel binds to the wrong occupant; undefined behavior per POSIX docs
entries.externally_observable_effect: results delivered to wrong request; canceled work reported done; memory corruption
entries.silent_or_distributed_character: silent and intermittent; classic ABA temporal window
entries.conventional_obligation: documented prohibition only: 'must not change / must not reuse while in progress'; no mechanical enforcement
entries.sluice_protocol_obligation: RequestKey = {ContextIdentity, SlotIndex, Generation} (include/sluice/async/detail/request_key.hpp:58); slot reuse bumps generation before the new occupant becomes visible; stale-generation requests are rejected by the arena/backend
entries.evidence_for_status: Public API cannot forge or reuse a stale RequestKey (identity is not caller-constructible; negative-compile gates scripts/verify-async-identity-negative-compile.sh, scripts/verify-request-arena-negative-compile.sh, scripts/verify-request-handle-authority-negative-compile.sh). Internally, stale-generation validation plus request-arena death tests witness rejection; TLA+ request-arena suite models generation discipline.
entries.comparison_notes: Same semantic slot-reuse hazard; conventional answer is documentation, Sluice answer is unforgeable identity + generation. T-S1a fact only; no migration claim.
se2_probe_candidates: death test for stale-generation dispatch under slot reuse
GenMC/TLA+ bounded reuse model already exists (request-arena suite)
entries.notes: Rejected candidate recorded: generic epoll user_data reuse anecdotes lacked causal in-flight identity binding; the aio control-block contract states the hazard precisely.

entries.title: Completion after close: in-flight operation races resource close (fixed-file UAF)

provenance.publication: Linux kernel io_uring CVE-2023-1872 (use-after-free, local privilege escalation)

sources.note: NVD entry: UAF in io_uring via io_file_get_fixed (CWE-416)

discoverer advisory: io_file_get_fixed missing ctx->uring_lock; async IORING_OP_SPLICE races fixed-file close/unregister -> UAF. The advisory's labeled 'primary fix' da24142b1ef9 was re-verified 2026-08-30 and is a different stable-only commit ('io_uring: ensure that io_init_req() passes in the right issue_flags'); not used as the fix record. Role corrected bug_record -> supporting in SE-1-CORRECTIVE-1 round 2 (review 5060124249 FIX 1): C0 must rest on a primary-authority incident record, which here is the NVD official_bug_corpus entry plus the verified upstream fix; the discoverer advisory annotates but does not establish the incident record.

verified 2026-08-30: 'io_uring: add missing lock in io_get_file_fixed' (Billy Jheng / STAR Labs; stable, committed 2023-03-03 by Greg K-H): locks the fixed-file lookup when invoked unlocked (io-wq) to avoid the race with fixed-file unregistration — exactly the CVE root cause. Commit message records the mainline fix was absorbed into the 5.18 file-assignment rework ('No single upstream patch exists for this issue').

normalized_semantic_trace: file F registered in the fixed-file table; operation O in flight referencing F
close/unregister path for F begins concurrently
O's lookup (io_file_get_fixed) takes a reference without the table lock
F's table entry is freed while O still uses it
O (or its completion) dereferences freed entry
use-after-free; exploitable for privilege escalation in kernel context
preconditions: lock-free lookup of a closeable resource
close allowed while operations in flight
entries.race_or_failure_window: between resource lookup and terminal CQE
entries.bad_outcome: use-after-free of the resource entry; completion touching dead state
entries.externally_observable_effect: kernel UAF / LPE (CVE scored); in user-space analogs, crash or data corruption
entries.silent_or_distributed_character: distributed race window; not silent when it crashes, but the causal close/in-flight pairing is easy to miss
entries.conventional_obligation: kernel-side: hold the registry lock for fixed-file lookup (the fix); user-side: do not close/unregister resources with operations in flight
entries.sluice_protocol_obligation: quiescent-destruction contract: destroying a backend/context with accepted/bound requests is a contract violation (named fail-fast, Debug+Release); nonnegative-but-closed fd is accepted and resolved by the real syscall (descriptor-validation rule), so completion-after-close of an fd cannot dangle backend state
entries.evidence_for_status: Scheduler teardown gates (begin_teardown) plus stranded-transit fail-fast exercised by scheduler teardown death tests (Debug+Release); uring close/drain mutation evidence docs/verification/phase-d4-uring-wait-close-drain-mutation-evidence.md (real-liburing mode, local execution).
entries.comparison_notes: Shares in-flight-operation-vs-resource-lifetime semantics (fixed-file entry freed under a live lookup/operation). Not mechanically demonstrated: a Sluice-side registered-resource slot lifecycle equivalent to the kernel fixed-file table (per-resource registry with refcounted lookup raced by close/unregister). Sluice's fail-fast covers live destruction of backend/context with accepted requests — an adjacent but not identical resource authority. Family mapping kept; comparability downgraded FAIR -> PARTIAL in SE-1-CORRECTIVE-1 (N1).
se2_probe_candidates: death test: destroy backend/context with accepted request → named fail-fast
real-backend close-while-in-flight probe (D2/D4 class)
entries.notes: Provenance corrected in SE-1-CORRECTIVE-1: bug record = NVD (official corpus) + STAR Labs discoverer advisory; upstream fix = stable commit 08681391 'io_uring: add missing lock in io_get_file_fixed', verified against the cited UAF (locks the fixed-file lookup raced by unregister). The advisory's labeled 'primary fix' da24142b1ef9 is a different commit and was not adopted; see the source notes. SE-1-CORRECTIVE-1 round 2: the advisory was demoted to a supporting source so that C0 rests only on primary-authority provenance (NVD official_bug_corpus/official-primary + stable fix 08681391/upstream-primary), as now enforced mechanically.

entries.title: Cancel vs complete: cancellation is best-effort and must not revoke an already-completing operation

provenance.publication: io_uring_enter(2) man page, IORING_OP_ASYNC_CANCEL semantics

sources.note: IORING_OP_ASYNC_CANCEL may return -EALREADY and 'the request may or may not terminate'; interruptible requests tend to cancel, already-started disk I/O generally cannot

normalized_semantic_trace: operation O accepted and possibly already executing
cancel attempt C is issued targeting O
O reaches its terminal concurrently (real result)
two candidate terminals now exist: C's canceled outcome and O's real result
if both publish, or C wins wrongly, the real result is lost or duplicated
caller observes contradiction (success + canceled, or double terminal)
preconditions: cancel issued while O is enqueued or running
entries.bad_outcome: lost real result, double terminal, or cancel acting on the wrong (reused) request
entries.externally_observable_effect: caller sees success and cancellation for the same op; accounting drift
entries.silent_or_distributed_character: distributed race; APIs document best-effort precisely because the window is real
entries.conventional_obligation: documented: cancellation is an attempt; the original operation may still complete normally; cancel CQE is evidence of an attempt, not an override of the result
entries.sluice_protocol_obligation: single terminal winner: WaitNode::resolve_ CAS (wait_node.hpp:350) and RequestArena terminal-winner arbitration; cancel paths record intent and can win a canceled terminal only where the protocol allows; loser never overwrites or double-publishes; cancel never publishes Completion-ready directly (reap-only publication)
entries.evidence_for_status: Second-winner protocol: resolve_ CAS makes a second outcome unwritable; e10-waitnode TLA+ suite models winner exclusivity; wait/resolve death tests; FE winner-law mutations (M1–M5) all RED in docs/verification/fe3-multi-frontend-mutation-evidence.md.
entries.comparison_notes: The conventional contract states the race exists and is tolerated; the Sluice protocol makes the invalid outcome (two terminals) unrepresentable. Detection-layer effectiveness is SE-2 work.
se2_probe_candidates: deterministic cancel-vs-complete race test (existing causal seam class)
e10-waitnode model as bounded witness

entries.title: Double terminal / double publication: duplicate CQE for one close request

provenance.publication: io-uring mailing list patch by Jens Axboe, '[PATCH] io_uring: fix sporadic double CQE entry for close' (2020-02-01); included in io_uring-5.6 pull

sources.note: Axboe diagnosis inside the patch record: punting close async assigned ->files, making io_close_finish() re-close and 'log a new CQE event for this request. This causes duplicate CQEs.'
same artifact contains the accepted fix (queue async work manually instead of returning -EAGAIN); dual-role same-artifact case, human-verified; applied in the io_uring-5.6 pull

normalized_semantic_trace: request O has two resolution paths (inline vs punted async)
a routing detail (file-table assignment) makes both paths believe they own the terminal
both paths emit a completion for O
one logical request produces two CQEs
caller consumes a phantom completion; req refcount drops twice
preconditions: two code paths can both reach the publication statement
entries.bad_outcome: duplicate CQE / double put of the request
entries.externally_observable_effect: extra completion event, refcount underflow, UAF on the request object
entries.silent_or_distributed_character: sporadic (per patch title); depends on async-punt routing
entries.conventional_obligation: exactly-once completion per accepted request; kernel needed a routing fix to restore it
entries.sluice_protocol_obligation: reap-only publication: only the designated reap path publishes Completion-ready (completion.hpp:404 publish_from_reap; src/async/threadpool_backend.cpp reap-is-sole-publisher rule); WaitNode::resolve_ CAS admits a single winner; teardown with stranded transit is fail-fast
entries.evidence_for_status: Single-winner CAS + single publication authority make double publication unwritable in the protocol; witnessed by e10-waitnode model, completion-authority death tests (scripts/verify-completion-authority-negative-compile.sh class), GenMC completion-publication kernels (spec/weakmem/completion-publication/).
entries.comparison_notes: Both are exactly-once publication obligations at the same abstraction level (runtime internal routing bug vs protocol law).
se2_probe_candidates: mutation: weaken resolve_ CAS → expect RED suite (already recorded as FE M-mutations)
GenMC publication kernel re-run

entries.title: Submit-failure rollback: partial submission leaves per-entry outcomes discoverable only via CQEs

provenance.publication: io_uring_enter(2) man page, RETURN VALUE section

sources.note: returns 'the number of I/Os successfully consumed'; 'The errors related to a submission queue entry will be returned through a completion queue entry'; only non-SQE errors surface as the syscall return

normalized_semantic_trace: caller submits N SQEs in one syscall
submission fails partway (or an entry is invalid)
syscall return does not identify which entries failed
per-entry errors surface asynchronously via CQEs
caller must reconcile return value + CQE stream to know what was accepted
incorrect reconciliation → leaked accounting, double retry, or lost work
preconditions: batch submission with per-entry failure possibility
entries.race_or_failure_window: syscall execution window (plus CQE arrival latency)
entries.bad_outcome: residue: accepted-but-unknown work, double-submitted ops, or lost requests
entries.externally_observable_effect: hangs (work lost), duplicate I/O, accounting mismatch
entries.silent_or_distributed_character: distributed between syscall return and asynchronous CQEs; easy to reconcile incorrectly
entries.conventional_obligation: documented: caller must treat submission count and per-entry CQE errors as separate channels and reconcile
entries.sluice_protocol_obligation: transactional submission: detail::submit_transaction ladder (include/sluice/async/detail/submit_transaction.hpp:95) commits all necessary bounded resources before accept; failed submit leaves no request, borrow, queue/kernel work, or accounting residue; post-accept enqueue does not depend on allocation (and post-terminal allocation failure is named fail-fast, exit 86 class)
entries.evidence_for_status: R2-ALLOC repair witnesses (PR #242: prepare-before-register rollback witnesses); FE PUB1/PUBCTL death tests for post-terminal allocation failure (docs/verification/fe3-multi-frontend-mutation-evidence.md); D2 uring failure-noalloc mutation evidence (docs/verification/phase-d2-uring-failure-noalloc-mutation-evidence.md, real-liburing local execution).
entries.comparison_notes: Conventional model exposes the reconciliation burden; Sluice moves the failure boundary before accept and fail-fasts the only residual window. Fairness caveat: Sluice has not been compared operation-by-operation against io_uring batch submission in a live experiment (that is SE-2/RE-1U territory).
se2_probe_candidates: fault-injected allocation failure at each ladder stage (existing R2 witness class)
uring partial-submission probe in real mode

entries.title: Partial / zero-progress I/O: retrying a partially completed write with different arguments corrupts the stream

provenance.publication: OpenSSL SSL_write(3) man page (partial write + moving buffer modes); Boost.Asio read_some/write_some short-I/O model

sources.note: after partial write 'it must be repeated with the same arguments' and 'The data that was passed might have been partially processed'; with SSL_MODE_ACCEPT_MOVING_WRITE_BUFFER 'the pointer can be different, but the data and length should still be the same'
read_some/write_some may transfer fewer bytes; composed operations loop

normalized_semantic_trace: write operation W transfers k < n bytes (partial success)
caller assumes all-or-nothing, or retries with a different buffer/offset
bytes [k, n) are resent from wrong location or duplicated
stream/logic-level corruption
or: zero-progress write is treated as retryable forever → livelock
preconditions: short-I/O semantics of the transport
caller-side retry logic
entries.race_or_failure_window: not a race — a semantic mismatch across the partial boundary
entries.bad_outcome: data corruption, duplicated bytes, or infinite retry livelock on zero progress
entries.externally_observable_effect: protocol corruption; hangs
entries.silent_or_distributed_character: silent at the I/O layer; manifests at the application protocol layer
entries.conventional_obligation: documented: after partial write, retry with identical arguments; zero progress must be treated as an error condition, not a retryable success
entries.sluice_protocol_obligation: public read_some/write_some semantics expose short I/O as typed Result outcomes; exact/all helpers loop on short results; non-empty write with zero progress is classified as backend failure, never retried forever (Result<T>/IoError vocabulary; docs/reference/api.md)
entries.evidence_for_status: Public sync/async API surfaces short I/O as explicit typed results (sluice_core Reader/Writer Result semantics); the silent partial-success variant is unrepresentable in the public contract. Caveat recorded in comparison_notes.
entries.comparison_notes: Sluice cannot stop a caller from ignoring a typed partial result; explicitness converts the silent hazard into a visible obligation, which is obligation-representation, not prevention. Zero-progress-as-backend-failure is a protocol rule; its dedicated death/segment tests are thinner than for other families — honest evidence gap noted for SE-2.
se2_probe_candidates: short-read/short-write loop helper tests (existing exact/all helper tests)
zero-progress write backend-failure probe
entries.notes: Supporting real-world adaptation: libcurl sets SSL_MODE_ACCEPT_MOVING_WRITE_BUFFER because its retry path can pass different buffer addresses (project source-level evidence; not claimed as C0).

entries.title: Timeout vs completion arbitration: linked timeout racing request completion (double free, io_uring 5.13 fix)

provenance.publication: Linux kernel io_uring linked-timeout completion race (syzbot-reported; Begunkov fix, mainline 447c19f, 5.13 merge window) + liburing linked-timeout contract

sources.note: '[PATCH] io_uring: fix ltout double free on completion race' (Begunkov, 2021-05-14): 'Always remove linked timeout on io_link_timeout_fn() from the master request link list, otherwise we may get use-after-free when first io_link_timeout_fn() puts linked timeout in the fail path, and then will be found and put on master's free.' Reported-and-tested-by syzbot; Fixes: 90cd7e424969d ('io_uring: track link timeout's master explicitly').

verified 2026-08-30 on the torvalds tree: mainline 447c19f3b5074409c794b350b10306e1da1ef4ba, fs/io_uring.c, merged via the io_uring-5.13 pull. Diff unlinks the timeout from the master's link list before the refcount grab, so the loser of the race is retired exactly once.

liburing io_uring_prep_link_timeout contract: the linked timeout constrains the linked request; 'if the linked request does not complete before the timeout, it is cancelled with -ETIME' — i.e. the contract itself defines the arbitration between timeout expiry and request completion.

normalized_semantic_trace: request R is submitted with a linked timeout T armed against it; the contract defines the intended arbitration: if R does not complete before T expires, R is canceled with -ETIME (liburing link-timeout contract)
R and T race: io_link_timeout_fn() fires while R is completing ('we race with the completion of the linked work' — fix commit)
exactly one final interpretation must win: R's real result, or R canceled -ETIME by T; the loser must be unlinked from R and retired exactly once

real bug: when the race hit the fail path, T was put by io_link_timeout_fn() AND later found still on R's link list and put again at R's free — double free/use-after-free (syzbot-reported; commit message)
fix: unlink T from R's link list before attempting the refcount grab, restoring single-winner arbitration (mainline 447c19f)
preconditions: linked timeout armed against an in-flight request
timeout expiry races request completion of the same linked pair
entries.race_or_failure_window: timeout expiry <-> request completion of the same linked pair
entries.bad_outcome: linked-timeout request freed twice (double put) -> use-after-free; two terminals claimed for one pair
entries.externally_observable_effect: syzbot-reported use-after-free/crash; memory corruption
entries.silent_or_distributed_character: distributed race window; intermittent (syzbot-class)
entries.conventional_obligation: exactly one final interpretation per timeout/request pair: the winner delivers its terminal (real result, or the loser canceled with -ETIME per the linked-timeout contract); the loser is unlinked and retired exactly once — the kernel needed a fix to restore this
entries.sluice_protocol_obligation: ordinary deadline authority centralized (AC-2b: arm/consume/retire_ordinary_deadline_locked, scheduler.hpp:2294/2305/2314); deadline expiry is one participant in the WaitNode resolve_ single-winner CAS, so grant and expiry cannot both win on the same wait; admission ladders are the single text of each primitive's admission
entries.evidence_for_status: Single-winner law for wait+deadline (e10/e9 model class; AC-2b mutation census 192 gates recorded in PR #238 evidence); same-object double grant/expiry is unwritable in the protocol.
entries.comparison_notes: Same-object winner race on both sides: the io_uring linked timeout is bound to the same request whose completion it constrains, and the fixed bug is exactly a double claim of the loser. Sluice's deadline participates in the same wait's single-winner CAS, so the equivalent invalid state (deadline and result both winning one wait) is unwritable. Evidence class is protocol/model/mutation census, not measured superiority.
se2_probe_candidates: deadline-vs-grant deterministic race tests (existing deadline choreography class in Condition/Select tests)
AC-2b mutation gates as sensitivity evidence
mutation: let the timeout path retire an already-resolved wait -> expect RED suite

The original draft anchor (connect(2) EINPROGRESS writability/SO_ERROR protocol) documents completion checking but not the timeout-vs-grant arbitration; its 'timeout raced a just-established connection' step was unsupported inference and is demoted to rejected_candidates. entries.title: Lost wake: pthread_cond_signal fails to wake a waiter (glibc condition variable bug)

provenance.publication: glibc Bugzilla #25847 with patch series (Malte Skarupke), discovered via 'Finding a bug in glibc's condition variable' analysis

sources.note: glibc Bugzilla: 'pthread_cond_signal failed to wake up pthread_cond_wait' (signal stealing via g_signals[] state)
patch series 'lost wakeup fix' (Malte Skarupke)
discovery analysis

normalized_semantic_trace: waiter W registers on condition variable CV and sleeps holding its waiter identity
signaler S evaluates the shared predicate and emits a wake
due to stale/incorrect published wake state, the wake is consumed by nobody (or attributed to a stale waiter)
W remains asleep with predicate satisfied
waiter is stranded indefinitely (liveness failure, not data corruption)
preconditions: wake state can desynchronize from live waiter set
entries.bad_outcome: lost wakeup; permanent or long-lived stall
entries.externally_observable_effect: hang; requires shutdown/restart
entries.silent_or_distributed_character: silent and intermittent; no data corruption signature, pure liveness
entries.conventional_obligation: wake obligations must pair persistent predicate/state with registration ordering so every registered waiter is woken exactly once
entries.sluice_protocol_obligation: wake epoch / persistent predicate protocol with terminal recheck (e9 park/wake model family); Q-LIV-1 opposite-role queue reconciler (grant_from_head_locked, scheduler.hpp:934–1152 region) reconciles cross-role FIFO heads; teardown never abandons registered waiters silently (stranded-transit fail-fast)
entries.evidence_for_status: The induced sibling of this exact family (SE1-SB-01 Q-LIV-1) was reproduced deterministically by the DST driver (PR #241 witness dst_t5_v1) and fixed with four regression witnesses (PR #242); e9 TLA+ suite historically exposed C++ park/wake epilogue gaps (PRs #190/#194).
entries.comparison_notes: Both are liveness-class lost-wake in a wait primitive. Sluice does not claim the class is impossible in implementation — its protocol + deterministic replay converts the historical silent bug into a reproducible, fixed one. That is a PAIR-D fact, not a superiority claim.
se2_probe_candidates: DST replay of queued wait/notify interleavings (existing dst_t5 class)
e9 model re-run on wake-path changes

entries.title: Shutdown with in-flight work: loop close refusal vs documented handler abandonment

provenance.publication: libuv loop API docs; Boost.Asio io_context destructor reference

sources.note: uv_loop_close: 'Releases all internal loop resources.' returns UV_EBUSY unless 'all open handles and requests have been closed'

entries.title: Durability/ordering confusion: fsync() error clearing makes retry-after-fsync-failure silently lose data (PostgreSQL fsyncgate)

provenance.publication: pgsql-hackers thread (Craig Ringer, April 2018) and PostgreSQL fsync fixes (data_sync_retry; Feb 2019 minor releases backpatched to 9.4–11)

sources.note: canonical project history page for the fsyncgate incident and fixes
release notes: new server parameter data_sync_retry controlling panic-on-fsync-failure (fix response)
on Linux, after fsync() reports EIO the page error state is cleared, so a later retry can return success though data was never written
analysis

normalized_semantic_trace: write W is buffered; fsync F1 fails with EIO; kernel clears the page dirty/error state
durability layer retries fsync F2 (or marks the page clean and retries later)
F2 returns success although the data never reached stable storage
durability layer reports the data durable
crash loses data that was reported durable — silent durability violation
preconditions: retry-after-fsync-failure policy
kernel error-clearing semantics
entries.bad_outcome: silent loss of reported-durable data; database corruption on crash
entries.externally_observable_effect: silent data loss after power/storage failure; for PostgreSQL, PANIC-on-fsync became the mandated response
entries.silent_or_distributed_character: fully silent: the wrong answer is a success code
entries.conventional_obligation: durability failures must be treated as unrecoverable (panic/recover-from-log), not retried; flush() ≠ durability; sync_data vs sync_all must not be conflated
entries.sluice_protocol_obligation: durability intent is explicit and split: flush() documented as not-durability; sync_data() (fdatasync) vs sync_all() (fsync) are distinct typed operations; sync errors surface as typed IoError with no retry loop (src/file.cpp do_sync: EINTR-only retry via the unified EINTR authority; WAL advances durable_lsn_ only on success, src/wal.cpp:212-216)
entries.evidence_for_status: No silent durability-retry machinery exists to get wrong: src/file.cpp:644-683 retries only EINTR and maps other errnos to typed failures; src/wal.cpp advances the durable marker strictly on success. The kernel error-clearing mechanism itself, however, operates below the Sluice boundary.
entries.comparison_notes: Overall pairing remains PAIR-X / COMPARABILITY_BLOCKED. Policy half = PARTIALLY COMPARABLE: fsync error -> should the application blindly retry, should the durability marker advance; Sluice has relevant behavior (non-EINTR sync errors propagate as typed IoError with no retry loop; durable_lsn advances only on success). Kernel-mechanism half = COMPARABILITY_BLOCKED: the kernel clears dirty/error state so a later fsync can succeed despite the lost write — that mechanism operates below the Sluice boundary and no user-space library obligation can represent it. Sluice does not solve fsyncgate; the policy half is represented, the kernel mechanism half is not (SE-1-CORRECTIVE-1 N2).
se2_probe_candidates: fault-injected sync failure probes asserting typed-error propagation and durable_lsn_ immutability (existing WAL test class)
documented boundary note: kernel cleared-error semantics are out of scope for any Sluice-layer probe
entries.notes: C2-class supporting artifact exists (OSDI'16 'All File Systems Are Not Created Equal' crash-consistency study) but was not required given the C0 primary record.

entries.title: Weak-memory publication: sleep/wake pairing requires full barriers (CPU 1 / CPU 2 store-then-load disagreement)

consumer C observes readiness and reads payload

consumer acts on unpublished or partially published state

schema_note: Schema v1 corrected in place while PR #245 was Draft (SE-1-CORRECTIVE-1, 2026-08-30): provenance.sources became structured {url, role, authority} records; entry_role / same_case_as / related_entries / root_cause_key were introduced; H08 was re-anchored to a verified upstream bug+fix. No schema v2 was created for a draft-only correction. Round 2 (same corrective authorization; PR #245 review 5060124249, 2026-08-30): C0 mechanically requires a primary-authority incident record; origin<->quality is a closed relation; authority repo-untracked (E4) introduced; SB-08 bucket corrected production-runtime -> internal/seam per the #227 hazard-bucket taxonomy; SB-10 reclassified OUT-OF-SE1 unconfirmed candidate. Still schema v1, still Draft-only.
population_law: POPULATION = corpus_eligibility == 'IN-SE1' AND entry_role == 'population-case'. Probe companions are artifacts, not denominator cases; OUT-OF-SE1 entries remain visible but are not denominator cases. This law drives the validator counts, the interpretation tables, and any future SE-2 matrix row population; SE-2 probes attached to companions attribute their result to the parent population case. Unconfirmed candidates — S0 entries whose repo evidence is exclusively repo-untracked (E4) — are OUT-OF-SE1 by law; they enter the population only when a later phase reproduces them into a formal entry, or they are explicitly dismissed.

source_role_contract.C0: >= 1 PRIMARY-AUTHORITY incident record (role bug_record or official_bug_corpus carrying authority upstream-primary or official-primary) AND >= 1 source with role upstream_fix. A supporting-authority bug_record annotates an entry but never establishes C0. The same artifact may carry both roles ONLY when it genuinely contains both the bug diagnosis and the accepted fix (encoded mechanically as the same URL listed under both roles; the dual-role claim itself is human-verified).
source_role_contract.C3: conventional-minimal by construction; no incident provenance required; sources must not claim bug_record/upstream_fix roles (no historical incident claim).
source_role_contract.S0: >= 1 source with role repo_evidence. An IN-SE1 population case requires >= 1 repo-primary (tracked, repository-established) source. Entries whose repo evidence is EXCLUSIVELY repo-untracked are UNCONFIRMED CANDIDATES and must be OUT-OF-SE1; they enter the population only when a later phase reproduces them into a formal entry.
source_role_contract.supporting: supporting sources may annotate any entry but never satisfy the C0/C1/C2/S0 role requirements.
source_role_contract.enforcement_boundary: scripts/verify-se1-hazard-corpus.py enforces MECHANICAL PROVENANCE SHAPE only. Whether a URL's content truthfully matches its claimed role, and whether the semantic mapping is valid, remain HUMAN SEMANTIC PROVENANCE REVIEW.
source_role_contract.repo-untracked: authority repo-untracked marks repository-side evidence that exists only in untracked human working-tree artifacts (E4 class). It records an observation without claiming tracked-repository establishment, and can never by itself establish population membership.

status_semantics: sluice_current_status is the PRIMARY DESCRIPTIVE OUTCOME FOR CORPUS NORMALIZATION ONLY. It is NOT the full detection profile: real detection layers overlap (an outcome recorded FAIL_FAST, DETERMINISTICALLY_REPRODUCIBLE, or TSan-detectable can co-occur for the same hazard). SE-2 owns the full hazard x detection-layer matrix; nothing in this corpus may be read as per-layer detection coverage.
